title: "Thought Leaders"

The people below are worth learning from. The first table is product management proper.
The two after it are the accounts worth following while you build, and the ones worth
following to understand where the field is heading.

Follow fewer accounts than you think. A short feed you actually read is more useful than a long
one you scroll past.

One thing to know before you build a feed: **application architecture has almost no social
media presence.** Nobody posts in depth about schema design, deploys, or CI. For that part
of the work, feeds will not help you and the docs and books in [Builder
Resources](https://byu-strategy.github.io/product-management/97-builder-resources.html) in the Product Management book are where to learn it.

## Who to follow while you build

The most useful accounts for building products with AI agents.

| Account | Why |
|---|---|
| [\@ClaudeDevs](https://x.com/ClaudeDevs) | Official Anthropic developer updates. Where Claude Code, API, and MCP changes get announced first |
| [\@bcherny](https://x.com/bcherny) Boris Cherny | Head of Claude Code. Agents, tooling, engineering workflow |
| [\@simonw](https://x.com/simonw) Simon Willison | Creator of Datasette, co-creator of Django. Near-daily practical posts. His [blog](https://simonwillison.net/) is the better resource, organized by tag |
| [\@steipete](https://x.com/steipete) Peter Steinberger | Built and sold PSPDFKit, now works on agents full time. Posts about advanced multi-agent setups. Not a first read |
| [\@emollick](https://x.com/emollick) Ethan Mollick | Wharton. Structured experiments on what AI is actually good and bad at. [One Useful Thing](https://www.oneusefulthing.org/) is the better subscription |
| [Every](https://every.to/): [\@danshipper](https://x.com/danshipper), [\@kieranklaassen](https://x.com/kieranklaassen), [\@every](https://x.com/every) | They ship AI products in public, Cora and Spiral among them, then write up what happened. Kieran on compound engineering is the most specific writing anywhere on agentic workflow |
| [\@HamelHusain](https://x.com/HamelHusain) Hamel Husain and [\@sh_reya](https://x.com/sh_reya) Shreya Shankar | The two people who turned evals into a teachable subject. Their free course is a good place to start on evals |
| [\@chipro](https://x.com/chipro) Chip Huyen | Wrote AI Engineering. Production systems, cost and latency tradeoffs |
| [\@swyx](https://x.com/swyx) | Links people and ideas across AI engineering, through Latent Space |
| [\@amanrsanger](https://x.com/amanrsanger) Aman Sanger | Cursor founder. The one framework account that bears directly on this stack |
| [\@alexalbert__](https://x.com/alexalbert__) Alex Albert | Anthropic, on prompting and agent behavior. The practice counterpart to \@ClaudeDevs announcements |
